title: Embeddings into Similarity Measures for Nearest Neighbor Search
authors: Alexandr Andoni (Columbia University, USA), Negev Shekel Nosatzki (Columbia University, USA)
abstract: We introduce the notion of metric embeddings into a {\em similarity measure} over $\R_+^m$, such as the weighted Jaccard coefficient. We develop {\em average} embeddings into such similarity measures for a number of metric spaces, with (appropriately defined) distortion that is smaller than the best possible or known distortion of embedding into $\ell_1$ or $\ell_2$ spaces (bi-Lipschitz or average). We complement our embeddings with a new algorithm for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) that leverages such an embedding in a black box fashion. Combining these results, we obtain new efficient algorithms for ANNS under the following two classic metrics, achieving an exponential improvement to longstanding prior work: 1) Edit distance over length-k strings: $\poly(\log k)$ approximation; 2) ℓ_p over $\R^d$, for $p>2$: $O(\log p)$ approximation (known to be asymptotically optimal in relevant models of computation).

I. I NTRODUCTION
In the classical problem of c-approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS), we need to preprocess a dataset P of
n points in some metric space X with distance function
d, so that, given a query point q ∈ X , we report a point
p ∈ P within distance c·minp∈P d(q, p). We study the highdimensional ANNS, which is motivated both by practice and
theory. ANNS has a wide range of applications for various
metrics which are typically high-dimensional; see, e.g., book
chapters [DK21], [SDI06], [TOG17]. Furthermore, ANNS,
as well as the tools behind the algorithms, are core primitives
in design of algorithms for high-dimensional questions,
frequently arising in the study of algorithms for massive
datasets; see, e.g., surveys [Ind01a], [And16] and specifically recent work on, say, density estimation [CKNS20] or
terminal embeddings [CN21]. See also the survey [AIR18]
for overview of the high-dimensional ANNS algorithms.
The algorithms for ANNS roughly fall into two classes:
direct algorithms, and via metric embeddings. Direct algorithms have been developed for a number of standard spaces,
notably `2 , `1 , `∞ , `∞ -product, `p , and general norms;

see survey [AIR18] references and more recent [KNT21],
[ANRW21]. Notably, some of the best algorithms for all
these metrics are based on data-dependent hashing — a type
of hashing or space partitions, which depend on the actual
given dataset P — in contrast to most of the early work on
ANNS which used data-independent (oblivious) hashing.
The second class of algorithm leverages bi-Lipschitz
metric embedding to reduce ANNS under some fixed metric
to ANNS under, say, `1 /`2 , or `∞ , for which we can use

Our results in the rest of the paper have the following

Each tree is build on the dataset P . Every node v corresponds to a subset of P , termed Pv . The root corresponds
